thread:
incident-bot: Pager: critical - api-serving 503 spike in us-east-1 - 20% error rate over 2m, alert rule: svc:api:5xx-rate
owen (oncall): I'm on it. switching to the incident channel. starting triage.
alex (sre lead): grabbing logs and recent deploys. @nora did we push a runtime change in the last hour?
nora (eng-runtime): no runtime deploys from infra in the last 3h. there was a canary model roll earlier at 18:02 UTC (not infra).
owen (oncall): reproducing locally - 503s look tied to tokenization service timeouts. increasing concurrency is showing queue backlog.
maria (product): what customers are impacted? any high-SLA contracts in the region?
ryan (cs): quick list: Acme Analytics (enterprise), Covalent Health (dedicated), 3 midmarket PLG customers. I'll pull invoice/SLA tiers.
jess (billing): flagging billing: if we determine a service credit is applicable, I need start/end window + affected customers list.
lina (support): fielding inbound tickets now, routing to priority. template needed for status update to customers.
alex (sre lead): mitigation plan: 1) scale tokenizer autoscaler + fallback to stateless tokeniser instance pool 2) route heavy customers to eu-west failover for small portion 3) temp increase timeout. executing 1 now.
own (oncall): executing scale, patching timeout to 10s. kicking off canary of pool change.
incident-bot: Deploy job started: autoscaler-scale-job #2045 by owen (oncall)
(2m later)
incident-bot: Deploy job succeeded: autoscaler-scale-job #2045 - 6 -> 18 instances
own (oncall): errors dropped to ~4% after scale. still seeing periodic spikes tied to a specific AV2 model variant.
nora (eng-runtime): digging into model variant. looks like KV cache thrash when sequence length > 2k from some customer prompts. adding cache guard to limit max_sequence for shared pool. patch in review.
alex (sre lead): good. we should prepare status page copy now reflecting current mitigation and impact window. Lina, can you post customer-facing language? use conservative ETA.
lina (support): draft status page: "We experienced elevated 5xx errors for text-generation in us-east-1 between 2026-03-15T18:01:30Z and 2026-03-15T18:44:50Z. Mitigation applied; services are recovered. Some requests may have seen increased latency or 5xx errors. We are evaluating impact and will follow up with customers about credits if eligible." thoughts?
maria (product): fine but call out that dedicated deployments were unaffected unless otherwise noted. add contact link.
lina (support): updated. posting to status page now.
incident-bot: STATUS PAGE UPDATE posted: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/RI-2026-0315-01
ryan (cs): I'll start outreach to Acme Analytics and Covalent Health with tailored note. draft: "We're investigating an elevated error rate in us-east that may have impacted your requests between 18:01 and 18:45 UTC. We're assessing impact and will share compensation details if eligible. Contact me directly for logs/LLRs."
jess (billing): For a service-credit assessment I need: confirmed start/end, whether the incident caused complete service loss or degraded requests, and per-customer request volume affected. Also need the signed SLA baseline (p99 latency, availability window).
own (oncall): Confirmed observation window: 2026-03-15T18:01:30Z -> 2026-03-15T18:44:50Z (approx 43m20s). health metrics show 5xx > threshold throughout.
alex (sre lead): note: small portion of requests retried successfully; not a total outage. recommend classifying as partial degradation for SLA purposes.
jess (billing): Under our SLA, credits are eligible for uptime below 99.5% per month per region. Need to compute per-customer touched minutes. Can someone export request logs and counts?
nora (eng-runtime): exporting filtered logs for us-east tokenization/timeouts and matching to customer IDs now. will attach counts in ~20m.
(10m later)
nora (eng-runtime): export done. attached: counts show Acme 12k requests in window (3.6% error), Covalent 1.2k requests (27% error), MidmarketX 400 requests (15% error).
jess (billing): rough credit calc: Covalent looks like primary candidate for credit given high error rate. Acme may not meet threshold but we'll compute exact SLA monthly impact. I'll draft a compensation proposal: 10% monthly credit for impacted region for Covalent, subject to legal signoff.
maria (product): hold on public comms about credits until we confirm with legal and sales. Ryan, loop in their AE.
ryan (cs): looping in AE now. @kumar do we need exec visibility?
kumar (cto): yes ping me on the customer drafts for Covalent (enterprise). Also notify partner ops.
own (oncall): mitigation completed and postmortem tracker created: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/RI-2026-0315-tokenizer-thrash - adding timeline and rollbacks.
alex (sre lead): action items: 1) nora complete cache guard hotfix and rollout to us-east by EOD 2) add additional telemetry to detect long sequences 3) ops run a monthly runbook to check tokenizer pool saturation.
jess (billing): I'll prepare a billing memo with proposed compensation language and amounts. will attach calculations and legal notes.
lina (support): final customer update (to send after billing/legal ok): "Update: issue mitigated as of 18:44 UTC. We apologize for disruption. We're evaluating eligibility for service credits and will follow up within 3 business days with next steps and any compensation."
ryan (cs): sent tailored note to Covalent and Acme (private thread). Covalent acknowledged and asked for log snippets and proposed credit.
jess (billing): shared initial compensation memo in thread. request legal review.
kumar (cto): thanks team. please ensure post-incident review includes why sequence length checks weren't earlier and improve model onboarding checklist.
alex (sre lead): agreed. closing watch window. will hand off to oncall rotation for monitoring until patch fully rolled. :thumbsup:
own (oncall): handing off to next oncall @owen-morning at 19:15 UTC. marking incident as recoverd->monitoring.
incident-bot: Incident channel will remain open for 24h for follow-ups.
